title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether deterministic verification plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). We document two preregistration/analysis issues evident in the archived artifacts: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per-condition generation, and (2) a prespecified comparison (GVR vs a schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no additional verifier-detectable benefit in this specific artifact-grounded setting; we release the authoritative archived artifacts and recommend reproducible follow-ups (independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model runs, and expanded verifier coverage).

sections.introduction: Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operator efficiency but raises operational safety concerns: stochastic generators may produce syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, required workflows, or security predicates). Prior work therefore recommends pipelines that interpose deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects before execution. We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment whose focal research question is: Does a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (GVR) reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to (A) unconstrained LLM generation and (B) schema-constrained decoding on a public synthetic NetOps task bank under the frozen execution contract? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered paired evaluation on 240 tasks using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic pybatfish-style validator with archived artifacts and deterministic reconciliation; (2) transparent artifact-backed accounting showing shared-initial-candidate semantics produced model_calls_used = 240 and that every generation satisfied the validator (n11 = 240); (3) confirmatory statistics (paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0], bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729); (4) identification and disclosure of two preregistration/execution mismatches that constrain inference and reproducible recommendations to restore discordance sensitivity.
sections.related_work:
We situate this run within three related lines. (i) LLM failure analyses and hallucination literature document that stochastic LLM outputs can be incorrect for code and structured artifacts, motivating deterministic validators in pipelines (survey and case studies summarized in the supplied evidence synthesis). (ii) Generate–Verify–Repair and constrained-decoding approaches have been shown to increase syntactic/executable output rates and reduce surface-level hallucinations; however, their measurable semantic benefit depends on verifier completeness and evaluation semantics. (iii) NetOps-specific work emphasizes verifier-driven evaluation (reachability/policy invariants), intent-translation prototypes, and human oversight as controls for high-stakes changes. Nearest-work comparison matrix (selected entries from the verified bibliography):
- Convergent Correctness / GVR discussion (R. Cadenas, 2026; DOI: 10.2139/ssrn.6754899): proposes generate–verify–repair architectures for deterministic validation; our run is a preregistered paired test of a bounded GVR variant against an archived synthetic task bank. 
- NetConfEval / intent→config evaluation (Changjie Wang et al., 2024; NetConfEval): provides NetOps task-bench motivation; our study uses a task-bank with explicit intent/policy predicates and deterministic validator traces. 
- MeshAgent (Zhou et al., 2025): a systems prototype integrating LLMs with network management validators; differs from our work by being a deployment-style system report rather than a preregistered paired experiment. 
This paper differs by (a) preregistration and a frozen paired analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), (b) archived deterministic reconciliation and full execution artifacts, and (c) explicit reporting of an executed generation_semantics choice (shared_initial_candidate) that deterministically removed within-pair stochastic discordance.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration, estimand, and frozen analysis: The study was preregistered as c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1 (preregistration SHA-256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (difference in verifier-detected semantic-violation proportion in paired design). Two primary comparisons were prespecified (C vs A and C vs B) with Bonferroni correction (family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). The frozen analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1. Experimental contract and implementation facts (archived): task bank: 12 clusters × 20 tasks = 240 paired tasks (planned_episode_count = 480). Requested generator: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Generation semantics executed: shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded single repair attempt); model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Analysis and reproducible artifacts: primary analysis inputs and outputs are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256: 36e13a0f35f75bdaf57b5304aedb8154b151ba261c7b53b4fa60563f12fd0a5f; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256: 09716238fc9ef042cf0ad4ab058aba93bf88180d74029ca5678655bcaddafded). Power/planned sensitivity: the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation; that assumption did not hold for the executed shared-generation semantics and therefore the preregistered power plan does not apply to the observed outcomes. Evidence-to-claim mapping (concise):
- "All planned episodes completed, model_calls_used = 240": execution_manifest completed_episode_count = 480; model_calls_used = 240 (execution_manifest representative artifact hashes; execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96...; execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 36e13a0f...).
- "Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier (n11 = 240) and no repairs applied": analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 09716238fc9e...; representative per-task scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (e.g., task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 841c8a13771344d0...) show validator validation_after.violation_count = 0 and validator_trace.repair_applied = false.
- "Preregistration present and frozen prior to execution": preregistration SHA-256 = eaedeae9aa30... (archived in manifest). 
- "Generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and deterministic reconciliation passed": execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 498eee5641a7... and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 733bdff79d35... (both archived).
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact-backed): planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; failed_episode_count = 0; complete_pair_count = 240; model_calls_used = 240 (shared-initial-candidate generation). Confirmatory contingency: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256: 09716238fc9e...). Summary rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 (paired_binary_analysis_v1); paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256: 3707b4022865...). Repair loop usage: validator_trace.repair_applied = false for every episode (representative scoring artifacts execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json and others). Unexecuted prespecified comparison: the preregistration foresaw two primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B); the archived execution contains only the adapter-configured paired experiment comparing unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared-initial-candidate semantics. No recorded rationale for omission of the schema-constrained baseline (B) comparison appears in the execution artifacts; we disclose this as a procedural deviation.
sections.discussion: Statistical and design interpretation: the observed degenerate contingency (zero discordant pairs) makes the paired McNemar test and bootstrap CI deterministic: p = 1.00 and CI collapsed to [0.0, 0.0]. This outcome is a direct artifact of two executed facts: (1) the generator+prompt pairing produced verifier-acceptable candidates for every task under the synthetic task distribution and verifier predicates, and (2) the shared_initial_candidate generation_semantics removed per-arm stochasticity and therefore removed within-pair discordance potential that a GVR intervention could reveal. Threats to validity (artifact-grounded): internal validity is limited by the preregistration/power mismatch (preregistration assumed independent per-condition generation but execution used shared generation); construct validity is limited by verifier completeness (passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 does not guarantee absence of all operational risks beyond encoded invariants); external validity is limited by the synthetic task bank, single model (gpt-5-mini), and single bounded repair budget; conclusion validity is limited because zero discordant outcomes preclude evidence for GVR efficacy under the executed semantics. Operational recommendations supported by the archive: (A) re-run the paired design with independent per-condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true) to restore discordance potential using the archived task manifest and RNG seeds; (B) inject adversarial/golden-reference tasks (preregistration planned 10% golden tasks) to validate verifier sensitivity; (C) broaden generator scope (multi-model) and increase repair-budget/iterations to assess iterative repair benefits; (D) expand verifier predicates or integrate symbolic/SMT checks to reduce oracle incompleteness (evidence_synthesis identifies integration with formal verification as an open gap). All recommended reruns can reuse the archived task manifest and adapter configurations to maintain deterministic traceability.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics and for the supplied model/prompt/verifier, every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), yielding a null paired estimate (0.0), exact McNemar p = 1.00, and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable value in this specific setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. Two preregistration/execution deviations materially constrain inference: (1) shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption; and (2) the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed with no recorded rationale. We therefore do not generalize beyond the specific model, prompt, task bank, verifier, repair budget, or generation semantics. We publish the authoritative archived artifacts to enable deterministic reruns that restore independent per-condition generation, adversarial injections, multi-model comparisons, and broader verifier coverage to robustly evaluate GVR’s operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
